name: Minecraft (Java Edition)
description: A Minecraft Java Edition server. Vanilla, Paper, Purpur, Fabric, Forge and NeoForge are the same blueprint with a different server build, so the world, backups and schedules survive changing your mind.

access.note: A Minecraft server has no web sign-in: players join with the Java Edition client at your host on port 25565. The port is published on loopback until you choose every interface under Runtime and allow it through the firewall. As shipped the whitelist is off and nobody is a server operator, so any Mojang-authenticated account that learns the address can join and build in your world.

provenance.updateNotes: The image is pinned to its Java 25 build, which current Minecraft releases need (26.x is compiled for Java 25 and will not start on Java 21); the server build itself is resolved at deployment from the upstream version API and recorded on the release.

inputs.name: server-type
inputs.label: Server software
inputs.description: Paper and Purpur accept Bukkit plugins. Fabric, Forge and NeoForge accept mods, and mods must match the server and the client.

choices.label: Vanilla
choices.description: The official server. No plugins, no mods.

choices.label: Paper
choices.description: A faster Vanilla-compatible server that accepts Bukkit plugins.

choices.label: Purpur
choices.description: Paper with more configuration, for people who want to change game rules.

choices.label: Fabric
choices.description: A light mod loader. Players need the same mods.

choices.label: Forge
choices.description: The long-standing mod loader for large modpacks.

choices.label: NeoForge
choices.description: The maintained continuation of Forge for current versions.

inputs.name: version
inputs.label: Minecraft version
inputs.description: Chosen from the versions the upstream API reports. Clients must be on the same version.

inputs.name: server-name
inputs.label: Server name
inputs.description: The line players see in their server list. Written into server.properties before the first start. Change it afterwards under Server settings, where the change survives restarts.

inputs.name: memory
inputs.label: Memory
inputs.description: Vanilla is comfortable at 2 GB. Large modpacks want 6 GB or more. This is guidance, not a player count.

inputs.name: max-players
inputs.label: Maximum players
inputs.description: Written into server.properties before the first start. Change it afterwards under Server settings, where the change survives restarts.

inputs.name: difficulty
inputs.label: Difficulty
inputs.description: Written into server.properties before the first start. Change it afterwards under Server settings, where the change survives restarts.

inputs.name: game-mode
inputs.label: Game mode
inputs.description: Written into server.properties before the first start. Change it afterwards under Server settings, where the change survives restarts.

inputs.name: whitelist
inputs.label: Whitelist only
inputs.description: With this on, only accounts you add can join. Written into server.properties before the first start. Change it afterwards under Server settings, where the change survives restarts.

inputs.name: online-mode
inputs.label: Verify accounts with Mojang
inputs.description: Turning this off lets anyone claim any username. Only do it behind a proxy that already authenticates. Written into server.properties before the first start. Change it afterwards under Server settings, where the change survives restarts.

inputs.name: pvp
inputs.label: Player versus player
inputs.description: Written into server.properties before the first start. Change it afterwards under Server settings, where the change survives restarts.

inputs.name: view-distance
inputs.label: View distance
inputs.description: The single biggest lever on memory and CPU. Written into server.properties before the first start. Change it afterwards under Server settings, where the change survives restarts.

inputs.name: simulation-distance
inputs.label: Simulation distance
inputs.description: Written into server.properties before the first start. Change it afterwards under Server settings, where the change survives restarts.

inputs.name: eula
inputs.label: I accept the Minecraft EULA
inputs.description: The server refuses to start without this, and the acceptance is recorded with your name and the time.

volumes.name: data
volumes.purpose: Worlds, server configuration, plugins and mods

secrets.name: rcon-password
secrets.label: Console password
secrets.description: How the dashboard's console and the graceful stop sequence reach the server. The image would otherwise generate one inside the container and write it only into server.properties.

files.label: Server properties
files.description: The server's own settings file. The fields below are the ones this dashboard knows how to edit safely; everything else stays in the raw preview.

automation.name: Nightly world backup
automation.description: Saves the world, then backs it up, every night at 04:00.

automation.name: Daily graceful restart
automation.description: Warns players, saves, and restarts to clear memory.

automation.name: Server update window
automation.description: The safe update order: warn, save, back up, update, then verify.

update.notes: Updating the server build never replaces the world. Rolling a release back restores the previous server build against the same data volume.
